newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SWEDBANK BUYS 7.4 PCT OF HOIUPANK'S SHARES.
newsitem.headline: SWEDBANK BUYS 7.4 PCT OF HOIUPANK'S SHARES.

text.p: Sweden's Swedbank said on Tuesday that it had signed an agreement with Estonia's central bank to buy 7.4 percent of Hoiupank's shares, raising its stake to 19.9 percent.
Swedbank's excutive vice-president, Lars-Oluf Odlund, told a news conference that the deal had been signed on Monday.
Odlund added that Swedbank has no intentions to further increase its stake in Hoiupank "for the time being".
A further increase of Swedbank's stake in Hoiupank would be based on the consensus of Hoiupank's management, Hoiupank's supervisory board said on Tuesday.
Hoiupank supervisory board chairman Joakim Helenius said his side had made no decision yet regarding a possible further increase in Swedbank's stake.
Swedbank last december bought 12.5 percent of the shares in Hoiupank.
"The Estonian central bank considers Swedbank to be a long-term strategic partner for Hoiupank...and thinks we will contribute to the development of Hoiupank," Odlund said.
Helenius said Hoiupank still planned to expand its activities outside of Estonia and the added involvement of Swedbank would help.
Hoiupank said earlier that it plans to enter Russia, Ukraine and the other Baltic countries.
Hoiupank is the second largest commercial bank in Estonia and its major shareholders besides Swedbank are the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the Estonian central bank.
